observation.visible_scene: A coastal beach scene at low sun (sunset or sunrise). The bright sun sits just above the horizon left of center, casting a vertical glittering reflection column across the water. A dark, vegetated headland/cliff occupies the right side, topped by a light-colored multi-story house. The sky is overcast with layered grey clouds. The foreground is a damp, pebbly sandy beach sloping to the waterline on the right. The overall framing of the sun, cliff, house and horizon stays fixed throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: A small, low wave develops in the lower-center/left of the water and translates shoreward (toward the bottom of the frame) over the clip; by the later frames it forms a thin white foam crest that advances diagonally onto the wet sand in the lower-left, spreading as it runs up the beach.

The sun's reflection path on the water shimmers and breaks into shifting bright/dark ripple segments frame to frame, but its column stays in the same horizontal position (this is reflection texture change, not a moving object).
The right-side waterline foam and the cliff/house silhouette remain essentially unchanged in position; no measurable motion of the sun, clouds, cliff or building is visible within the ~2.7 s window.
The camera appears largely static: the horizon, cliff edge and house hold the same screen positions from first to last frame, with only negligible handheld-level jitter.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the sun is rising or setting, and its longer-term vertical movement, is not determinable from this short segment.
Whether the incoming wave fully breaks, completes its swash, or recedes after the last frame is unseen.
Any motion or context before the first frame (wave onset) is outside the excerpt.
The cause of the wave (wind, swell set) is not shown.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is treated as effectively static, but a very slight handheld drift cannot be fully ruled out given the fixed background.
The exact moment the lower-left wave begins to crest is gradual; only the shoreward translation and foam formation are clearly supported.
Distinguishing tiny ripples in the glitter path from real water-surface deformation is approximate.
